summary: s2.3 gives most volumes, temperatures and cycling for the clip, purification, assembly and transformation steps. It does not give the volumes or concentrations of the Biolegio linkers and DNA parts in each 30 µl clip reaction, and the full procedure is deferred to the supplementary DNA-BOT instructions, which I may not use. Without those amounts the clip stoichiometry cannot be set defensibly, and I could not recover them from a permitted source. My web-tool quota ran out before I could fetch the Storch 2017 chapter or the Biolegio linker datasheet, which might have supplied them.

gaps.detail: Volume and concentration of each Biolegio half-linker (prefix and suffix) added per clip reaction, and the volume of each 200 ng/µl part (or ng of DNA) added per clip reaction
gaps.why_needed: The clip reaction is 20 µl master mix plus linkers, parts and water to 30 µl, so 10 µl is left for the DNA components. Linker-to-part stoichiometry determines clip efficiency and so assembly accuracy. Part stocks are 200 ng/µl, but the volume used and the working concentration of the linker plate are not stated.

gaps.detail: Heat-shock details for the NEB 5-alpha 96-well plate (C2987P): heat-shock time and temperature
gaps.why_needed: The paper only says 'according to the manufacturer's instructions'.
gaps.resolution: For the 96-well plate, heat shock for 10 s at 42°C. NEB notes that 30 s loses about 40% of transformation efficiency. Cells are supplied at 20 µl per well, with SOC outgrowth medium provided.

gaps.detail: Volume of assembly reaction added to the 20 µl competent cells, and the ice incubation times before and after heat shock
gaps.why_needed: The paper adds 125 µl SOC 'to each assembly' but does not say how much of the 15 µl assembly goes into the cells. The ice times are also not stated.
gaps.resolution: Thaw the plate on ice and add the assembly to the cells. NEB recommends 1–5 µl of DNA, and a 15 µl assembly is above that range, so use about 5 µl. Incubate on ice for 30 min, heat shock 10 s at 42°C, then put back on ice for 5 min. Add 125 µl SOC and incubate 1 h at 37°C with the lid off, as the paper states. The ice times come from NEB's general C2987 protocol, which is written for the single-tube formats rather than the plate.

gaps.detail: Bead clean-up details: bead–reaction mixing and binding time, magnet settling time, number of ethanol washes, ethanol removal and drying time, and H2O resuspension volume and time
gaps.why_needed: The paper gives only 54 µl beads per 30 µl clip, 150 µl 70% ethanol per wash and 38 µl of eluate transferred.
gaps.resolution: Use standard SPRI practice: mix and bind for about 5 min, then 2–5 min on the magnet. Do two 70% ethanol washes and dry for about 2–5 min. Resuspend in about 40 µl H2O, incubate for 2–5 min, return to the magnet and transfer 38 µl of supernatant to a fresh plate.

gaps.detail: Plate incubation after spotting (temperature and duration), and the clip and assembly water volumes
gaps.why_needed: Colony growth conditions are not stated in s2.3. Assembly buffer volumes for each of the up to 10 parts are also not stated.
gaps.resolution: Spot 5 µl or 10 µl on the OmniTray with 40 ml LB-agar and 25 µg/ml chloramphenicol. Let the spots dry, then incubate inverted at 37°C overnight (about 16–18 h). For the assembly, mix 1.5 µl of each purified clip into the 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 10 mM MgCl2, 50 mM KCl buffer, with the buffer making up the remainder of the 15 µl.
gaps.source: standard practice; assembly composition from s2.3

gaps.detail: Plate layout of parts, linkers and constructs for the 88 designs, and the robot deck set-up and script parameters
gaps.why_needed: Needed to place each part and linker in the correct well and run the four OT-2 scripts.
gaps.resolution: Figure 3a defines the 88 constructs: full promoter × RBS permutations in two gene orders, minus the weak J23105/RBS1 GFP combination. The csv files and DNA-BOT_instructions_v1.0.0 are deferred supplementary files and were deliberately not consulted. The layout must be rebuilt from the design in Figure 3a; wells A12–H12 hold the backbone and no-plasmid controls.

retrieved_details: NEB 5-alpha Competent E. coli 96-well plate (C2987P): 20 µl cells per well, stored at -80°C, SOC outgrowth medium supplied (https://www.neb.com/en-us/products/c2987-neb-5-alpha-competent-e-coli-high-efficiency). Optimal heat shock for the 96-well plate is 10 s at 42°C, and 30 s loses about 40% of efficiency (https://www.neb.com/en-us/faqs/2013/03/11/what-is-the-optimal-heat-shock-time-for-the-96-well-plate-format-neb-5-alpha-competent-e-coli-neb). NEB's general C2987 protocol (written for the single-tube formats): thaw on ice, add 1–5 µl DNA containing 1 pg–100 ng, flick to mix without vortexing, 30 min on ice, heat shock, 5 min on ice, then SOC outgrowth (https://www.neb.com/en-us/protocols/high-efficiency-transformation-protocol-c2987?pdf=true). The Storch 2015 BASIC paper (https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/99356aa9-ec30-4a95-b15e-20b6f4f58849/content) says the protocol is in its Online Supplementary Information, which was not retrievable. The Storch 2017 chapter (https://link.springer.com/protocol/10.1007/978-1-4939-6343-0_6) is paywalled, so clip linker and part amounts could not be recovered. Details given in s2.3: clip master mix is 3 µl 10× Promega T4 ligase buffer + 1 µl NEB BsaI-HF v2 + 0.5 µl Promega T4 ligase per 20 µl reaction, with 20 µl per clip. Clips are 30 µl total with linkers, parts and water. Cycling is 20× (37°C 2 min, 20°C 1 min), then 60°C 5 min. Purification uses 54 µl AMPure XP, 150 µl 70% ethanol per wash, and 38 µl eluate transferred. Assembly is 15 µl with 1.5 µl of each purified clip in 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 10 mM MgCl2, 50 mM KCl, at 50°C for 45 min. Transformation uses 125 µl SOC and 1 h at 37°C with the lid off. Spotting is 5 µl (or 10 µl for the Figure 3b plate) on an OmniTray with 40 ml LB-agar and 25 µg/ml chloramphenicol.
